definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sliding door or room divider made of a wooden frame covered with thick paper or cloth.

examples.japanese: {襖|ふすま}を{開|あ}けて{隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: I opened the sliding screen and went into the next room.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{襖|ふすま}を{張|は}り{替|か}えた。
examples.english: I had the old fusuma re-papered.

examples.japanese: {襖|ふすま}の{絵|え}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{画家|がか}が{描|えが}いたものだ。
examples.english: The painting on the fusuma was done by a famous artist.

notes:
{襖|ふすま} are traditional Japanese sliding doors used as room dividers in Japanese-style rooms. Unlike {障子|しょうじ}, they are opaque.

COMPARISON:
- {襖|ふすま}: Opaque sliding screen (thick paper/cloth)
- {障子|しょうじ}: Translucent sliding screen (thin paper that lets light through)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {襖|ふすま}を{開|あ}ける (to open the fusuma)
- {襖|ふすま}を{閉|し}める (to close the fusuma)
- {襖|ふすま}を{張|は}り{替|か}える (to re-paper the fusuma)
- {襖絵|ふすまえ} (painting on fusuma)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{襖|ふすま} can feature elaborate paintings and are sometimes valuable works of art, especially in temples and historic buildings.
